articles.title: The election changes Washington. The work on crypto continues
articles.snippet: The next Congress inherits an unfinished assignment: establishing clear, lasting rules for digital assets that protect consumers and ensure American innovation continues to thrive, writes Blockchain Association's Lindsay Fraser.

articles.title: Bitcoin rebounds from midterm dip as DeFi leads gains
articles.snippet: Bitcoin recovered from a dip to around $75,600 as Democrats won Congress, while DeFi tokens led gains and Trump-linked coins fell.

articles.title: Trump-linked tokens lead crypto losses after Democrats sweep in the US midterms
articles.snippet: The official Trump and World Liberty Financial tokens were the two biggest losers among the top 100 cryptocurrencies on Wednesday, even as Bitcoin and Ether rallied.

articles.title: SpaceX blocks tokenized stock listing on OKXICE despite offshore trading boom
articles.snippet: SpaceX joined several other issuers objecting to OKXICE tokenized trading, months after crypto platforms offered tokens tied to its shares.

articles.title: Anthropic's AI Is Getting Cheaper to Use. That's Becoming a Problem for Its Business
articles.snippet: Claude's prices are falling, but Anthropic's computing expenses grew faster than sales in the latest quarter—a tricky equation ahead of its IPO.
